To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a new member of the myc proto-oncogene family, designated MYCL2, which is related to MYCL and is located on chromosome Xq22----q28, and that the MYCL2 gene is not amplified in lung tumors.
we have characterized a DNA sequence that is homologous to the myc gene and that this DNA sequence maps to the long arm of X chromosome.
A MYCL1 related gene (MYCL 2) was isolated and mapped on the long arm (q22----q28) of the human X chromosome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, isolation and characterization of a new processed gene, MYCL2, that maps to Xq22----q28 and is highly related to MYCL2.
the isolation and characterization of an MYC-related sequence that has homology to MYCL1, a processed gene that is frequently amplified in small cell lung cancer.
the characterization of a new member of the MYC gene family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MYCL1 gene family consists of at least three members, MYCL1, MYCL2, and MYCL3 (L-MYC), which are located on chromosomes 1, X, and 1, respectively.
the sequence of MYCL2 is related to L-MYCL1, is located on the long arm X chromosome in band q22----q24, and is a processed gene.
MYCL2 is a processed gene related and homologous to MYCL1, which is localized on the long arm (bands q22----q24) of the X chromosome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MYCL2 is an X-linked processed pseudogene with homology to MYCL1.
MYCL2 is a processed gene related in sequence, structure, and expression to MYCL1, and is located in an X-linked gene cluster of proto-oncogene sequences.
MYCL2 is a processed gene related closely to MYCL1 and that it maps on the long arm X chromosome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MYCL2 is a processed gene with strong homology to MYCL1, and that the MYCL1 gene family is located in the same chromosomal region.
there is a processed gene related closely to MYCL1, and that it is located on the X chromosome.
MYCL2 represents a new processed X-linked member of the myc family.
